title: Accusative 5: He, She, Them
description: Personal pronouns have unique accusative forms: меня, тебя, его, её, нас, вас, их.
descriptionRussian: Личные местоимения имеют особые формы в винительном падеже: меня, тебя, его, её, нас, вас, их.
intro: Everything so far could be worked out by looking at a word. Pronouns cannot. There is no ending to read and no gender to check; there are eight forms, and you either have them or you do not. That sounds like a step backwards and is not, because these eight are among the most-used words in Russian. You will reach for меня and тебя more often than for any noun in this book. Learn them now and they stop costing you anything.
rules: Personal pronouns have unique forms in the accusative. They are not regular: я → меня, ты → тебя, он → его, она → её, оно → его, мы → нас, вы → вас, они → их.
Just like English uses 'me, you, him, her, us, them' as direct objects (not 'I, he, she, we, they'), Russian uses these special forms whenever the pronoun is the WHAT or WHOM of the action.

Heads up: его means BOTH 'him' (accusative of он) AND 'his' (possessive). Same for её ('her' as object vs 'her' as possessive). The verb tells you which one. If a verb is acting on the pronoun, it is the accusative.
examples: Я люблю тебя. (I love you.) ты → тебя.
Маша знает меня. (Masha knows me.) я → меня.
Антон видит её. (Anton sees her.) она → её.
Мы помним их. (We remember them.) они → их.
Вы понимаете нас? (Do you understand us?) мы → нас.

items.promptEnglish: I am listening to a song.
items.hint: Recap from lesson 3: feminine -я ending changes to which letter in the accusative?
items.explanation: Recap from lesson 3: feminine -я swaps to -ю in the accusative. Песня → песню. Today we shift to pronouns, which don't follow gender-ending rules at all. They have their own memorized forms.

items.hint: In English you say 'Anton loves ME' (not 'I'). What is the Russian equivalent?
items.explanation: Just like English uses 'me' (not 'I') as a direct object, Russian uses меня: Антон любит меня.

items.hint: ты becomes which form when it is the object of a verb?
items.explanation: Pronouns do not follow the noun rules you learned in earlier lessons. They have their own forms that you have to memorize. Ты → тебя.

items.hint: Watch out: его has two meanings. Here it follows the verb видит, so it is the object.
items.explanation: его is the accusative of он. Important warning: его also means 'his' (possessive), so you have to read the sentence carefully. When a verb is acting on the pronoun (Лена видит ___), его means 'him'.

items.hint: она becomes which form as a direct object?
items.explanation: она → её in the accusative. Same warning as его: её can also mean 'her' as a possessive ('её брат' = her brother). After a verb, it means 'her' as the object.

items.hint: Plural pronouns also have their own forms. они → ?
items.explanation: Plural personal pronouns each have their own accusative form, just like the singular ones: мы → нас, вы → вас, они → их. There is no rule, just memorization.

items.hint: Use the informal 'you'. ты becomes which form as a direct object?
items.explanation: Just like English says 'I love YOU' with an object pronoun, Russian uses the accusative form: ты → тебя. Я люблю тебя.

items.hint: она becomes which form when it is the object of видит?
items.explanation: она → её in the accusative. When a verb is acting on the pronoun, её means 'her' as the object: Антон видит её.

items.hint: мы becomes which form as a direct object?
items.explanation: мы → нас in the accusative: Маша понимает нас. The plural pronouns each have their own memorized form: мы → нас, вы → вас, они → их.

blanks: Маша слушает _____. (Masha is listening to us.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Choosing the correct accusative pronoun by meaning. Мы (we) → нас (us).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha has known you for a long time.
errorCorrection.explanation: Personal pronouns have unique accusative forms. Вы is the nominative form, used only when 'you' is the subject of the sentence ('вы знаете?', 'do you know?'). As a direct object, вы shifts to вас: 'Маша знает вас.'

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон каждый день видит вы в коридоре.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton sees you in the corridor every day.
errorCorrection.explanation: Вы is the nominative form, used only when 'you' is the subject. As a direct object, вы shifts to вас: 'Антон видит вас.'

errorCorrection.sentence: Лена давно любит он, но никогда ему не сказала.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena has loved him for a long time but has never told him.
errorCorrection.explanation: Он is the nominative form, used only when 'he' is the subject. As a direct object, он shifts to его: 'Лена любит его.'

reviewVocab.definition: personal pronoun (я, ты, он, она, мы, вы, они)
reviewVocab.example: Я, ты, он — это личные местоимения.

reviewVocab.definition: whom? (the accusative question word for people; drilled with nouns in the next lesson)
reviewVocab.example: Кого ты видишь? — Я вижу его.
Я знаю его. (I know him.) / Это его книга. (This is his book.)
